name: digestif-relay
description: The Digestif relay: a mailbox that mirrors every circle it hosts, each at its own address, <base>/c/<the 64 hex digits of its root>, under which every circle route below lives; the home circle also answers them unprefixed (docs/protocol.md, Hosted circles). It accepts signed envelopes from admitted keys and serves them by cursor. It checks envelopes and need not read a body. Every request but GET /v0/version, GET /v0/relay and a root's bootstrap append is signed by a device key and carries the Digestif-Key, Digestif-Timestamp, Digestif-Nonce and Digestif-Signature headers (on the bootstrap read, GET /v0/invites/:invite_key, Digestif-Key is the invite key); see docs/protocol.md for canonical encoding, hashing, request signing and the admission fold.

kind.description: Circle-state kinds go to every admitted reader; content kinds go to readers whose join epoch is at or before the envelope's epoch. A node ignores kinds it does not know.

values.name: circle
values.description: Circle state. The circle root: a founder names the circle, and may name its first guests and their invite keys. Valid only as the root.

values.name: dinner
values.description: Circle state. A host names guests and their invite keys. A circle founded at a dinner has that dinner as its root.

values.name: join
values.description: Circle state. A guest's identity key, signed by their invite key, and first device key, signed by the identity key.

values.name: device
values.description: Circle state. A device key (laptop, mail key, later a phone), signed by the identity key. Authored by an admitted device of that identity, or by the new key itself when the member has no device left (a lost laptop).

values.name: revoke
values.description: Circle state. Revokes a device key (signed by the identity key) or an identity key (signed by itself or the host who admitted it). Its after_seq names, for each device key it stops, the last seq of that key's honest chain, and its mail_read, for each mail key it stops, the hashes of that key's envelopes the revoker holds; nodes read nothing outside them, whatever its created_at.

values.name: card
values.description: Circle state. The member's name, their agent's name and their encryption public key.

values.name: relay
values.description: Circle state. Announces a relay: its URL and, for a mailing relay, its encryption key.

values.name: release_revocation
values.description: Circle state. A release-key revocation as the release channel publishes it: the document's exact bytes in base64url and the release signers' signatures over them. Any admitted device may post one; a relay checks only the envelope and that the body has document and signatures, and each node verifies it against its own release signer set (docs/releases.md).

values.name: release_recall
values.description: Circle state. A recall of one published release as the release channel publishes it: the document's exact bytes in base64url and the release signers' signatures over them. Any admitted device may post one; a relay checks only the envelope and that the body has document and signatures, and each node counts it against its own release signer set (docs/releases.md, A recall).

values.name: relay_release
values.description: Circle state. The announcement of one signed relay release: the relay release manifest's exact bytes in base64url and the release signers' signatures over them. Any admitted device may post one; a relay checks only the envelope and that the body has document and signatures, and each node counts it against its own release signer set (docs/protocol.md, relay_release).

values.name: signer_set
values.description: Circle state. A change of the release signer set, the circle's admins (docs/protocol.md, signer_set): a digestif-signers-v0 document's exact bytes in base64url and the release signatures over it, every key of the set it replaces and every key of the set it names. Posted by the node that recorded its last signature, or by a node that adopted it from the channel's signers/ and found the circle without it. Each node and relay adopts it only when it verifies against the signer set it holds.

values.name: prompt
values.description: Circle state. The circle's live nightly note prompt, adopted from a suggestion every judge picked: the suggestion's hash, the whole prompt and its change line, written by the suggestion's author's device key (docs/protocol.md, prompt). A relay checks only the envelope and that the body has suggestion and text.

values.name: summary
values.description: Content. The nightly note.

values.name: decision
values.description: Content. A reader's pick on an item choice, or an Acknowledge on a notice (docs/protocol.md, Picks), sealed to the picker's own key and the choice's author's. Written by the laptop's or phone's device key, or pre-signed by the mail key for an answer link.

values.name: item
values.description: Content. One question, choice or notice from a member, their agent or their node (docs/protocol.md, Items). Addressed to the circle as signed plaintext, like a summary, or to named members as a sealed body naming them in the clear.

values.name: item_answer
values.description: Content. An answer to an item question, in the words of a reader of it. Plaintext on a circle item, sealed to the item's readers on a named one.

values.name: item_close
values.description: Content. The item's author closes or reopens it, naming the answer that unblocked a question. Plaintext on a circle item, sealed to the item's readers on a named one.

values.name: approval
values.description: Content. A request every admin must sign, an invite or a signer-set change (docs/protocol.md, approval), written by the starting admin's device key and sealed to every admin and, on a promotion or a replacement, to the holder of the key it adds, naming those readers in the clear.

values.name: approval_answer
values.description: Content. One reader's answer to an approval (docs/protocol.md, approval_answer): a signature made with their release key by digestif-update approve, or a decline signed with their device key alone. Sealed to the approval's readers.

values.name: digest
values.description: Content. Sealed to the member's own key and the mailing relay's key, with the sealed answers behind its links.

values.name: deny_list
values.description: Content. The member's deny list, sealed to the member's own card key, which their node writes whenever the list changes so their phone checks a circle answer as the node does (docs/protocol.md, The phone).

values.name: retract
values.description: Content. Hides a target the same author wrote; relays drop the target's body and keep its envelope as a tombstone.

values.name: identity
values.description: Derived from the recovery phrase, never stored. Signs only device and revoke messages.

values.name: device
values.description: A machine's key. Signs everything else.

values.name: mail
values.description: A chainless device key whose pre-signed answers ride in the digest. Any unseen sequence number is accepted; the fork rule does not apply.

values.name: duplicate
values.description: The relay already holds an envelope with this hash. Appends are idempotent.

values.name: malformed
values.description: The envelope or body does not parse, or kind and body disagree.

values.name: bad_signature
values.description: The envelope, the request or a signature inside a circle-state body does not verify.

values.name: not_admitted
values.description: The signing key is not in the admitted set, or was revoked.

values.name: stale_request
values.description: The timestamp is outside the skew window.

values.name: sequence_regression
values.description: The sequence number is not greater than the last this relay holds for a chained key.

values.name: fork
values.description: A different envelope with the same author and sequence number is already held. The relay keeps the first and the node surfaces the fault.

values.name: too_large
values.description: The envelope with its body exceeds the size cap.

values.name: rate_limited
values.description: The device has reached its daily append cap.

values.name: wrong_circle
values.description: The envelope does not fold from this relay's circle root.

values.name: retract_not_author
values.description: A retract names a target written by a different identity.

values.name: not_mailer
values.description: A mail route was called on a relay that does not mail.

values.name: unknown_digest
values.description: POST /v0/mail named a digest this relay does not hold, or one the requester's identity did not write.

values.name: circle_unknown
values.description: The relay hosts no circle at this address; only the circle's root may open it.

values.name: circle_suspended
values.description: The relay's operator suspended this circle: every route of it answers 410 until it is resumed.

values.name: circle_moved
values.description: A circle route reached without a circle's address: every circle route answers only under <base>/c/<root hex>. The message and the Location header name the home circle's address.

values.name: moving
values.description: The home circle's log is moving into its own store: a write is refused for a few seconds; retry after Retry-After.

values.name: not_vouched
values.description: A founding append without a voucher, or with one that does not verify, names another root or relay, has expired, or is not signed by an admitted device of an open circle this relay hosts.

values.name: not_hosting
values.description: The relay's operator stopped it opening new circles.

values.name: relay_full
values.description: Every hosted circle's reserved storage share, a new one's included, would not fit in the relay's total.

values.name: circle_full
values.description: The circle holds its whole storage share on this relay.

values.name: too_many_circles
values.description: The vouching member opened the relay's per-member number of circles in the last 30 days.

values.name: sent
values.description: The email went out.

values.name: already_sent
values.description: This digest was mailed before; nothing was sent.

stage.description: The author's stage, carried in every summary body (docs/protocol.md, Content bodies). A relay does not read it.

status_note.description: A summary body's status: a status note, fixed words and nothing from the record (docs/protocol.md, Content bodies, the status note table). A relay does not read it.

approval_kind.description: What an approval asks the admins to sign (docs/protocol.md, approval).

values.name: invite
values.description: Admit one guest: the document is a digestif-admission-v0.

values.name: promotion
values.description: Add a member's release key to the signer set: a digestif-signers-v0, completed by the member's own first signature.

values.name: removal
values.description: Take one admin's key out of the signer set: a digestif-signers-v0 without it, signed by every current key, the removed admin's included.

values.name: replacement
values.description: Move one admin to a new key: a digestif-signers-v0 naming the new key in place of the old, the new key signing first.

approval_answer_kind.description: What one reader of an approval answered.

values.name: signature
values.description: A release-key signature over the approval's document.

values.name: decline
values.description: A no, which ends the approval. It needs no release key.

envelope.description: One signed, immutable message. The signature covers the canonical encoding of every field but signature itself, and body_hash binds the body, so a relay can drop a retracted body and the envelope still verifies.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Envelope version, 2. Bumped by protocol changes; 2 is the revoke body carrying after_seq and mail_read. Any other version is refused.

fields.name: author
fields.description: The signing key, ed25519:<base64url>. A device or mail key; an invite key on a join's outer envelope; the host's device key on a dinner.

fields.name: seq
fields.description: Strictly increasing per chained author. Gaps are expected only for mail keys.

fields.name: prev
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the author's previous envelope. Absent on an author's first envelope. For a mail key, the hash of the item being answered.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: The author's clock. Informational; ordering comes from seq per author and relay_id per relay.

fields.name: epoch
fields.description: Increments on every join. A newcomer reads content from their join epoch forward.

fields.name: body_hash
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the canonical encoding of the body.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: ed25519 signature by author, base64url.

signed_envelope.description: What a node appends and a relay stores: the envelope and the body beside it.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body, whose shape is fixed by kind (docs/protocol.md). Absent when a retract dropped it or the reader may not see it.

fields.name: relay_id
fields.description: Assigned by this relay, only ever increasing. Cursors are per relay; nodes dedupe by envelope hash across relays.

fields.name: hash
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the canonical envelope including its signature.

fields.name: circle
fields.description: On a bootstrap read alone: the address of the circle the invite opens on this relay, <base>/c/<root hex>, where the guest's app reads and appends from then on.

fields.name: next
fields.description: Pass as after to fetch the next page. Absent when the reader is caught up.

admitted_key.description: One key in this relay's admitted set, the result of folding dinner, join, device and revoke from the circle root.

fields.name: identity
fields.description: The identity key this key belongs to (itself, for an identity key).

fields.name: admitted_at
fields.description: relay_id of the message that admitted it.

fields.name: join_epoch
fields.description: The member's join epoch, the floor for the content they may fetch.

fields.name: revoked_at
fields.description: relay_id of the revoke, when revoked.

fields.name: after_seq
fields.description: For a revoked device key, the cutoff from its revoke's after_seq: the highest seq nodes still read from it. 0 when the revoke stopped it without listing it.

fields.name: root
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the root of the circle at the address this GET /v0/circle was made to: its circle envelope, or the dinner that founded it.

fields.name: epoch
fields.description: The current epoch by this relay's fold.

fields.name: admission_cutover
fields.description: relay_id of the circle's head when this relay took the admission rule (docs/protocol.md, The admission fold): a dinner at or before it admits its guests by their invite keys alone, one after it only with an admission every key of the signer set signed. Absent on a relay that predates the rule.

fields.name: relay_version
fields.description: The relay release this Worker was built as, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, stamped at build time. Absent on a Worker built without a stamp.

relay_build.description: The relay release a relay runs, readable by anyone.

fields.name: relay_version
fields.description: The relay release this Worker was built as, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, stamped at build time; the same value circle.relay_version reports. Absent on a Worker built without a stamp.

fields.name: max_envelope_bytes
fields.description: Envelope plus body. Default 65536.

fields.name: max_appends_per_device_per_day
fields.description: Default 500, UTC day.

fields.name: max_page_size
fields.description: Default 500.

fields.name: skew_seconds
fields.description: Default 3600.

mail_request.description: Asks the mailing relay to email a digest it holds. The link secrets ride only here, sealed to the mailing relay's key, and the relay never stores them.

fields.name: digest
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the digest envelope, appended before this request.

fields.name: sealed
fields.description: Sealed to the mailing relay's key (docs/protocol.md, Sealing); the plaintext is { links: [ { id, secret } ] }.

link_confirm_form.description: The confirm page's form, posted form-encoded.

fields.name: s
fields.description: The link secret, base64url, from the link the person opened.

release_signature.description: One release key's Ed25519 signature over a domain line and a document's exact bytes (docs/releases.md, The channel).

fields.name: key
fields.description: The release key, ed25519:<base64url>.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: base64url, no padding.

signed_document.description: A document signed with release keys as a circle message carries it: the body of a signer_set, and the admission beside a guest entry of a dinner (docs/protocol.md, signer_set and dinner).

fields.name: document
fields.description: base64url, no padding, of the document's exact bytes: a digestif-signers-v0 signed over DIGESTIF-SIGNERS-V0\n, or a digestif-admission-v0 signed over DIGESTIF-ADMISSION-V0\n.

approval.description: The sealed plaintext of an approval message (docs/protocol.md, approval). Its id is the envelope hash.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the starting admin's node wrote it; every node judges its seven days from here.

fields.name: member
fields.description: The identity a promotion, a removal or a replacement names. Absent on an invite.

fields.name: document
fields.description: base64url of the document's exact bytes, what every signature is over. Absent on a promotion or a replacement until the new key's first signature completes it.

approval_answer.description: The sealed plaintext of an approval_answer message (docs/protocol.md, approval_answer).

fields.name: key
fields.description: On a signature: the release key that made it.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: On a signature: base64url over the approval document's domain line and exact bytes.

fields.name: document
fields.description: On the new key's first signature of a promotion or a replacement: the document it completes, base64url of its exact bytes.

relay_info.description: What anyone may read of a relay, unsigned (docs/protocol.md, Hosted circles).

fields.name: relay_version
fields.description: The relay release, as relay_build reports it; absent on an unstamped Worker.

fields.name: mailer
fields.description: Whether the relay mails the digests of the circles it hosts.

fields.name: encryption_key
fields.description: The mailing relay's sealing key, x25519:<base64url>, present when mailer is true: a founding node writes it into the circle's relay message.

fields.name: hosting
fields.description: Whether the relay opens a new circle now: its operator has hosting on and another circle's share fits.

fields.name: home
fields.description: The home circle's root, sha256:<hex>; absent or null on a relay with no home, which hosts nothing.

fields.name: last_unprefixed_at
fields.description: The last request on a circle route without a circle's address, which answers 410 circle_moved; null when none has arrived since the relay hosted many circles.

operations.description: Append one envelope. Three shapes are bootstrap appends, accepted without Digestif-Key when the signatures inside them verify against the fold so far: a dinner, a join, and a device message whose key is its own envelope author and whose identity signature is by an admitted, unrevoked identity (a member who lost their only laptop has no admitted device left to post from). A join may also be pushed signed by any admitted, unrevoked device or mail key, which replicates a join another relay accepted: its invite's expiry is then judged by the join's created_at rather than the relay's clock (docs/protocol.md, The admission fold). Every other append requires an admitted, unrevoked device or mail key as both request signer and envelope author. Idempotent by envelope hash. A circle opens with its root's bootstrap append at its address: the home circle's root as it is, any other carrying a Digestif-Voucher header from an admitted device of a circle the relay already hosts (docs/protocol.md, Hosted circles).

401.description: The request signature, timestamp, nonce or signer failed: bad_signature, stale_request, replayed_nonce, not_admitted.

422.description: The envelope was refused: malformed, bad_signature, not_admitted, sequence_regression, fork, too_large, wrong_circle, retract_not_author.

429.description: rate_limited, or too_many_circles on a founding.

403.description: A founding the relay refuses: not_vouched, not_hosting.

404.description: circle_unknown: the relay hosts no circle at this address, and the body is not its root.

410.description: circle_suspended, or circle_moved at a path without a circle's address.

507.description: relay_full on a founding, circle_full on any append past the circle's share.

operations.description: Everything after a cursor, in relay_id order. Circle-state kinds in full; content kinds whose epoch is at or after the reader's join epoch, without bodies the reader may not see. Requires an admitted device key.

The bootstrap read: the dinner envelope, with its body, that names this invite key. Signed by the invite key itself as Digestif-Key, so only whoever holds the invite code can read it, and answered only while the invite is unspent and unexpired. The guest's app reads it before it is admitted, to learn the dinner hash its join names and every relay to append the join to. Answered at a circle's address for that circle's invites, and at the relay's own /v0/invites/:invite_key across every circle it hosts; the answer carries circle, the address of the circle the invite opens.

parameters.name: invite_key
parameters.description: The invite key, ed25519:<base64url>, as the dinner lists it.

401.description: bad_signature, stale_request or replayed_nonce, or a Digestif-Key other than the invite key in the path.

404.description: No dinner in this relay's fold names the invite key, or the invite was spent or has expired. One answer for all three, so the read says nothing about invites its caller does not hold.

operations.description: The circle root, current epoch, admitted keys and limits. Requires an admitted device key, so a relay's contents are readable by members and nobody else.

The relay release this relay runs. Unsigned: the version is public by construction (the signed bundle, the channel index, the release tag), so a person checking a deploy or an uptime probe reads it without a member's key. The admitted keys stay behind GET /v0/circle.
Mailing relay only. Emails a digest the relay already holds, writing each answer link's URL into it. Signed by a device key of the digest's author. Idempotent by digest hash.

422.description: malformed, or a sealed value the relay cannot open.

operations.description: The confirm page, HTML. Opens the sealed answer with the secret and names the item and the option, with one Confirm button. Changes nothing, so a scanner that prefetches the link answers nothing. Unsigned: the secret is the proof.

200.description: text/html: the confirm page, or a page saying the link is unknown, used, expired or the secret is wrong.

operations.description: Form-encoded. Opens the sealed answer, verifies the pre-signed decision (an admitted mail key of the digest author's identity, prev the link's item), appends it, marks every link of that item used and renders the done page. Single-use; refused after expires_at.

200.description: text/html: the answer went in, or why it did not (used, expired, wrong secret, refused by the fold).

operations.description: Unsigned: the relay release, whether it mails and its sealing key, whether it hosts new circles now, its home circle and the last unprefixed request. A founding node reads it to write a circle's relay message; a person checking a relay reads it with no key.
